builder_plan.scenario: Tool errors or unavailable services cause your agent to abandon recoverable tasks.
builder_plan.change: Inject repeatable tool failures and change only the recovery policy.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retry and fallback behavior under the same injected failures.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Recovered tasks, duplicate side effects, retries, time to recovery, and total cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Language Models Steer on Injected Uncertainty Tokens, but Fail to Self-Monitor In Situ
summary: This replaces self-verbalized stepwise confidence as the trigger for backtracking in agentic reasoning, which the paper shows fails as a monitoring signal, with external detection of error steps followed by injection of an explicit low-confidence token or rethinking instruction. The cost is an additional error-detection component (a verifier, separate model pass, or heuristic) plus extra generation for revised continuations, adding latency and API spend, and the self-monitoring prompting itself provides no usable signal. Injected doubt can cause the model to discard already-correct reasoning, reducing solve rates by up to 22.8 points, so the approach fails when the external detector produces false alarms on sound steps.
rationale: The finding is directly actionable on a single GPU or API: abandon reliance on self-verbalized confidence as an error signal and instead drive repair from an external verifier or scripted doubt injection, while validating on your own workload that injected doubt does not destroy correct traces.
technique: Externally injected uncertainty for error repair

claims.statement: This replaces self-verbalized stepwise confidence as the trigger for backtracking in agentic reasoning, which the paper shows fails as a monitoring signal, with external detection of error steps followed by injection of an explicit low-confidence token or rethinking instruction. The cost is an additional error-detection component (a verifier, separate model pass, or heuristic) plus extra generation for revised continuations, adding latency and API spend, and the self-monitoring prompting itself provides no usable signal. Injected doubt can cause the model to discard already-correct reasoning, reducing solve rates by up to 22.8 points, so the approach fails when the external detector produces false alarms on sound steps.

Injecting a 10% confidence tag at an error step raises downstream correction by +3.7 to +22.5 points over format-matched 95% certainty (up to 38.5% with active rethinking instructions); self-verbalized confidence, however, is near chance at detecting errors (AUROC 0.500–0.561).
